text:
rachel: quick note: observed streaming latency histogram showing a persistent 300ms offset for a single edge pool after the midnight rollout. looks like timestamps are shifted vs ingress. anyone else?
aj: noticed that too. traces show that the `ingest_received_ts` vs `route_handled_ts` delta is ~280-320ms for pool-edge-5. suspect clock drift on that pool.
kevin: confirmed via node probe: ntp drifted ~300ms on 3 hosts after an autoscale event that introduced nodes with incorrect ntp config. that explains the bucket shift into 250-600ms.
maria: UX impact: users see 300ms in histogram which inflates perceived client latency. we should surface a 'timestamp drift' annotation and offer an option to use server-side corrected latency (route_handled - ingest_received) instead of raw report.
ops-bot: alert: pool=edge-5 clock-drift>200ms detected; auto-remediation scheduled: restart nodes to re-sync NTP.
rachel: short-term: can we add a console overlay that shows `timestamp_drift_ms` per-edge so oncall can quickly spot this vs real latency? also add rollout annotations when new nodes join a pool.
aj: long-term: prefer to compute latency using server-corrected deltas and expose the raw vs corrected toggle. Implementation: attach `server_received_ts` at routing and compute latency in ingest before bucketing. cheap and fixes drift issues.
kevin: agree. also need a guard: if server-corrected delta <0 or >5s mark as suspect and surface in UI.
console-bot: created ticket #UI-3032 "expose server-corrected streaming latency + timestamp-drift overlay" assigned to eng-platform + eng-infra.
maria: follow-ups: aj to prototype ingest-side corrected-latency calculation; kevin to patch node bootstrap to enforce NTP config and drain bad nodes; rachel to add UI mockup for the toggle and drift chart.
(00:25) kevin: remediation kicked off; nodes restarted and clock drift resolved. latency histogram returned to baseline.
rachel: thanks. let's add the corrected-latency default for histograms during rollouts so users aren't spooked by infra clock flakiness.
